Complete case study: morphological prey remains in pellets or scats

Source: vignettes/articles/case-study-morphological-remains.Rmd
case-study-morphological-remains.Rmd

Research question, sample frame and limitations

This example asks which prey remains were recorded in a collection of pellets and how the picture changes when we distinguish records, estimated numbers of individuals and sample-based occurrence.

The pellet survey is simulated; its observations do not describe a real predator, location or feeding process. Pellets, regurgitates, scats and stomachs can share a data structure, although preservation and digestion affect each material differently. Recovered remains therefore cannot be treated as a complete measure of ingested biomass.

Sampling unit: one pellet, with a unique pellet_id even when the same bird or site was sampled repeatedly. Record: one prey category observed in that pellet. Count: a minimum number of prey individuals estimated from diagnostic remains, not the count of otoliths, feathers or fragments.

library(DietView)
set.seed(412)
frame <- data.frame(
  pellet_id = sprintf("PEL%02d", 1:24),
  predator = rep(c("Illustrative predator A", "Illustrative predator B"), each = 12),
  season = rep(rep(c("spring", "autumn"), each = 6), 2),
  site = rep(c("Site1", "Site2"), 12)
)
classification <- data.frame(
  prey_name = c("Clupea harengus", "Crangon crangon",
                "Unidentified fish", "Unidentified animal remains"),
  kingdom = rep("Animalia", 4),
  phylum = c("Chordata", "Arthropoda", "Chordata", NA),
  class = c("Actinopteri", "Malacostraca", NA, NA),
  order = c("Clupeiformes", "Decapoda", NA, NA),
  family = c("Clupeidae", "Crangonidae", NA, NA),
  genus = c("Clupea", "Crangon", NA, NA),
  species = c("Clupea harengus", "Crangon crangon", NA, NA)
)
i <- rep(seq_len(nrow(frame)), each = nrow(classification))
j <- rep(seq_len(nrow(classification)), times = nrow(frame))
minimum_individuals <- stats::rpois(length(i), lambda = c(1.5, 1.2, 0.8, 0.4)[j])
minimum_individuals[i %in% c(1, 14)] <- 0L  # deliberately empty sampled pellets
records <- cbind(frame[i, ], classification[j, ],
                 n_individuals = minimum_individuals)
records <- records[records$n_individuals > 0L, , drop = FALSE]
rownames(records) <- NULL
frame$empty <- !(frame$pellet_id %in% records$pellet_id)
head(records[, c("pellet_id", "predator", "prey_name", "n_individuals")])
#>   pellet_id                predator                   prey_name n_individuals
#> 1     PEL02 Illustrative predator A             Crangon crangon             2
#> 2     PEL03 Illustrative predator A             Clupea harengus             5
#> 3     PEL03 Illustrative predator A           Unidentified fish             2
#> 4     PEL04 Illustrative predator A             Crangon crangon             3
#> 5     PEL04 Illustrative predator A Unidentified animal remains             2
#> 6     PEL05 Illustrative predator A             Clupea harengus             2

Validate the long table and examined-sample inventory

The inventory must keep the two sampled pellets with no prey records. Otherwise they disappear from the long table and the proportion of sampled pellets with detections is exaggerated. A real zero needs a clear field protocol: an empty bag, an uninformative sample or a pellet with no identifiable remains may represent different states.

stopifnot(!anyDuplicated(frame$pellet_id))
stopifnot(!anyNA(records$pellet_id), all(records$n_individuals > 0))
stopifnot(!anyDuplicated(records[c("pellet_id", "prey_name")]))
c(examined = nrow(frame), with_remains = length(unique(records$pellet_id)),
  without_remains = sum(frame$empty))
#>        examined    with_remains without_remains 
#>              24              22               2
spec <- dv_spec(predator = "predator", stomach = "pellet_id",
                prey_name = "prey_name", count = "n_individuals",
                unit_label = "pellet", covariates = c("season", "site"))
prep <- dv_prepare(records, spec, taxonomy = "columns",
                   stomachs = frame, empty_col = "empty", verbose = FALSE)
prep
#> <dietview_prep>
#>   records   : 53 
#>   pellets   : 22 
#>   predators : 2 
#>   ranks     : kingdom > phylum > class > order > family > genus > species 
#>   covariates: season, site 
#>   source    : columns 
#>   examined  : 24 pellets, 2 empty

The rank columns are explicitly assigned for the simulated data; do not make up family/species names to fill missing ranks in real samples. When you have only prey names rather than ranks, resolve them with WoRMS/GBIF and audit their matches, or use a checked frozen lookup table.

Quantities: records, individuals, and occurrence

With one row per taxon and pellet, record share reflects how frequently categories appear among the observed records; it is not a sample-based frequency of occurrence. DietView can also sum the estimated number of prey individuals via currency = "numbers". Only use that option if the counts really estimate individuals, rather than fragments or sequencing reads.

tree_records <- dv_tree(prep, currency = "records")
tree_numbers <- dv_tree(prep, currency = "numbers")
rec <- dv_rank_table(tree_records, "Class")
num <- dv_rank_table(tree_numbers, "Class")
head(rec[, c("label", "pct_occ")])
#>          label  pct_occ
#> 5 Malacostraca 32.07547
#> 6  Actinopteri 26.41509
#> 7           NA 22.64151
#> 8           NA 18.86792
head(num[, c("label", "pct_occ")])  # numerical share (%N)
#>          label  pct_occ
#> 6  Actinopteri 34.88372
#> 5 Malacostraca 31.39535
#> 7           NA 17.44186
#> 8           NA 16.27907

pct_occ is the column name in either tree; its meaning is recorded by the currency attribute, so report it as record share or numerical share (%N) accordingly.

The denominator of %FO must be declared. Here, all 24 pellets were examined, and the inventory includes the empty ones.

fo_nonempty <- dv_fo_table(prep, rank = "class",
                           denominator = "nonempty")
fo_examined <- dv_fo_table(prep, rank = "class",
                           denominator = "examined")
head(fo_nonempty[, c("taxon", "n_stomachs", "n_total", "pct_fo")])
#>          taxon n_stomachs n_total pct_fo
#> 1 Malacostraca         17      22  77.27
#> 2           NA         16      22  72.73
#> 3  Actinopteri         14      22  63.64
head(fo_examined[, c("taxon", "n_stomachs", "n_total", "pct_fo")])
#>          taxon n_stomachs n_total pct_fo
#> 1 Malacostraca         17      24  70.83
#> 2           NA         16      24  66.67
#> 3  Actinopteri         14      24  58.33

The n_stomachs and n_total names in DietView’s output are historical interface labels; for this analysis they count pellets, not stomachs. %FO across prey categories need not add to 100%, because a pellet can contain multiple taxa.

Visualization and unidentified remains 

dv_sunburst(tree_records, mode = "occurrence",
            title = "Morphological pellets (simulated)",
            subtitle = "Share of prey-category records, unidentified included")

A white wedge below Chordata represents the observed fish fragments that could not be placed at class or a finer rank. Material assigned only to Animalia is even less resolved. Neither category should be silently dropped and the remainder rescaled to 100%.

dv_resolution(prep, by = "season")
#>   season finest_rank n_records weight p_records p_weight
#> 1 autumn     Kingdom         6      0  20.68966       NA
#> 2 autumn      Phylum         6      0  20.68966       NA
#> 3 autumn     Species        17      0  58.62069       NA
#> 4 spring     Kingdom         4      0  16.66667       NA
#> 5 spring      Phylum         6      0  25.00000       NA
#> 6 spring     Species        14      0  58.33333       NA

This is taxonomic resolution, not a calibrated digestion index. Do not use dv_digestion_diagnostic() unless genuine, interpretable digestion stages were recorded for the sampled units or prey remains.

Export with explicitly represented empty pellets 

m <- dv_matrix(prep, rank = "family", currency = "fo",
               include_empty = TRUE)
c(pellets = nrow(m), columns = ncol(m))
#> pellets columns 
#>      24       3
stopifnot(nrow(m) == nrow(frame))
head(rowSums(m))
#> PEL02 PEL03 PEL04 PEL05 PEL06 PEL07 
#>     1     2     2     2     3     3
utils::write.csv(m, file.path(tempdir(), "pellet_presence_matrix.csv"))

Here currency = "fo" produces a 0/1 pellet × prey category matrix. A zero is no recorded remains in that pellet, not proof the prey was not eaten. The sampling inventory retains the two observed empty pellets as all-zero rows; a blank or failed laboratory examination should instead be flagged as unknown, not automatically counted as empty.

dv_build_html(prep,
  output = file.path(getwd(), "pellet_remains_demo.html"),
  bands = "occurrence", currency = "numbers", strata = "season",
  title = "Simulated pellets: minimum prey individuals")

Scientific interpretation and transfer to real pellets or scats

Report how units were collected, repeated observations from the same predator, identification rules, the anatomical basis of minimum individual counts, empty/failed samples, the taxonomic resolution, %FO denominator, all exclusions, and measurement uncertainty. Distinguish fragment frequency, minimum prey counts, and recovery probability. Digestion resistance and preservation can make hard parts overrepresented. For DNA-derived scats, do not reuse the minimum-individual workflow: use the DNA case study instead.
